category_title: Youth with intellectual disabilities who thrive in hands-on retail environments
minimal_context: Eric is sitting in the classroom completing paperwork to prepare for an upcoming test.
dialogue:
TUTOR: Eric, please sit down and start working on this paperwork to prepare for the upcoming test.

STUDENT: I don't want to do this. I like hands-on learning, not just sitting here.

TUTOR: Please just focus on the worksheet in front of you.

STUDENT: But school is just a place where we sit down and just do paperwork. It doesn't teach me any skills.

TUTOR: You need to know this information for the exam. Keep reading.

STUDENT: (Pushes the paper away) No. I'm just going to learn this for your test and then forget about it. I want to do something real, like prepare for an interview.

options.A: Have the student complete the paperwork on an iPad by tracing along the screen with their finger.
options.B: Self-monitor specific praise and deliver it to the student on a two-minute fixed interval schedule using a praise self-monitoring form.
options.C: Provide opportunities for the student to learn about occupations through community placements that match their needs and interests.
options.D: Provide a communication book composed of a typed conversational opener with a corresponding Picture Communication Symbol for the student.
